Software developers frequently encounter bugs while coding, often spending excessive time identifying and fixing them. Although various testing tools exist to help detect bugs, their effective use requires familiarity with each tool's specific features, which is difficult for different tools. Our work aims to assist the community by integrating numerous testing tools, including 17 different ones as of now, into a unified platform that provides a consistent interface. This platform, CUTE-test, includes an automated algorithm that can identify bugs in code and suggest corrections, thereby facilitating the discovery of new insights. Since its inception in July 2022, the system has verified over 93% of more than 250,000 test suites, leading to the correction of 3,125 bugs and the publication of 110 new research papers. In addition to verifying test suites, the platform also identifies defects in widely-used scientific libraries, contributes to their fixes, and aids in finding improvements to the test suites themselves. By streamlining the process of accessing various testing tools, our system is designed to accelerate the discovery of knowledge, potentially benefiting the scientific community in ways that may even require little integration effort.

G_K-Artin-Scheier extensions represent a crystalline G_K-extension model that parallels G_K-Ramifications G_K-Artin-Scheier extensions in their structural and computational aspects, showing no changes when transitioning to reductions modulo p.

Engineering critical components made of self-sensing composite materials can mitigate accidents by enabling real-time damage detection through embedded fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensors. However, noise in sensor data can hinder accurate rupture identification, necessitating a noise-reduction approach based on self-organizing maps and a optimization strategy combining genetic algorithms and maximum likelihood estimation to enhance signal fidelity. The efficacy of this methodology has been validated using both simulated and experimental tests on a smart composite beam, demonstrating its efficacy in improving signal-to-noise ratio and accurate damage detection capabilities.

A new approach to proving Weyl's and Beck's integral identities is presented through vector geometry, with proofs provided using Green's Theorem. By employing modified geometric vectors, the Weyl-Beck identities are extended to incorporate a vector-valued function, and an additional identity is proven.

A right-angled Artin group acting on a tree results in a core-free subgroup subgraph, where two group members commute if and only if they translate in parallel within the tree. A subgraph is deemed derived from a single tree angle if it can be obtained from the tree through a sequence of operations, where a splitting operation involves cutting the tree at an edge and growing it into a Y-shape, while a leaf removal simply cuts off a Y-shape's end. Recently, White and Windland showed that every possible tree angle is in some power of two steps away from a basic tree through a combination of splitting and leaf removal operations. We define a subgraph to be tangle-free if no part of it translates into a Y-shape after acting on the tree. Then, for right-angled Artin groups, any subgraph that results from a submatrix with a block diagonal structure can be acted upon in a tree shape, where Y-shape producing subgraphs are irrelevant, if the graph in question is not completely connected. Additionally, a subgraph resulting from a submatrix that corresponds to a diagram with one irreducible segment and two components when divided by that segment is also tangle-free, provided the involved components aren't connected to each other through every possible node.

This paper Nested Neumann algorithm is proposed for solving systems of equations that are linear but not consistently positive definite and requires no inverse of a subset of the matrix to be available even in cases where some parts of the matrix are positive definite and others are not. The Nested Neumann algorithm is shown to converge under relatively mild conditions that can be easily verified, especially if the system's inception depth is known. Systems of equations that are linear but not consistently positive definite are shown to be resolved effectively for various matrix patterns and step sizes, and are shown to be useful for estimating the end of sequences that are decreasing but not at known limits, including estimating the end of multiplicative sequences.

We establish new, information-theoretic limits on the minimum bits required among a system's components in contextual linear bandits. Notably, we demonstrate that without any prior knowledge about the context distribution, a logarithmic bit growth is unavoidable. Conversely, with even a minimal amount of context distribution knowledge, we prove that constant bit growth can be achieved. Building on these theoretical insights, we introduce novel algorithms: LiOWA and LiCWEA, offering polynomial time horizon regret bounds, and a nearly optimal log time horizon regret bound under specific conditions. Our findings fill a critical knowledge gap and provide an optimal understanding of the role initial context diversity plays in contextual linear bandits.

To accurately predict the cooling efficiency in protoplanetary disk regions beyond a star's dust formation line, a cooling curve that extends to extremely low temperatures is necessary. An updated dust thermal properties model is presented that incorporates reasonable heat capacities at very low temperatures and includes data for various particle sizes and compositions. According to this model, micro-meter sized silicate particles retain significant heat even at temperatures near absolute zero, while smaller, oligomeric dust particles cool more efficiently at temperatures below 10 Kelvin. To validate the model, radiative equilibrium codes were developed and tested using various initial conditions and inputs, showing consistent results with previous studies. Outer regions of protoplanetary disks are found to be highly sensitive to dust thermal properties, as seen in the cooling efficiency graphs for different particle sizes and compositions. To account for extremely low temperatures, cooling curves beyond the formation line are necessary, and the决定 factor for cooling efficiency in outer disk regions is whether the temperature can be reached based on balance between heating sources and cooling efficiency.

This research focuses on harmonic functions defined on gradient shrinking Ricci solitons that exhibit polynomial growth of a specific degree. By proving a polynomial growth condition implies a higher power polynomial growth condition, a Liouville-type theorem is derived, indicating that a harmonic function with polynomial growth on a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton is actually of a specific polynomial growth rate. This research builds on the work of multiple scholars, including Schoen-Yau, Cheeger-Yau, and others, and is particularly relevant to recent findings by Xiao and Zhu, and Zhu.

Neural networks typically classify data into predefined categories, creating challenges when implementing dynamic backdoor attacks that affect specific characteristics rather than predefined classes. Unlike traditional backdoor attacks that route activated backdoors to a fixed target class, dynamic attacks require the malicious classifier to contact a controlling server to determine the target class at inference time, which is susceptible to various disruptions such as target class leakage, server outages, and overheads. To address these issues, we propose two efficient dynamic backdoor attacks, TDB and CDB, that minimize the need to contact the controlling server and can be classified as a fixed target backdoor with the ability to behave as a dynamic target upon activation. Our experiments on multiple image datasets demonstrate that both TDB and CDB attacks achieve nearly identical performance to traditional static target attacks while also demonstrating the ability to classify new tasks at the triggering label with minimal overheads. Furthermore, a composite experiment reveals that the activated backdoor can behave as a regular target backdoor or a dynamic target backdoor, dictated by the status of the controlling server.

This research introduces a novel, decentralized learning algorithm for distributed data environments, inspired by a random movement method used in computer science. The purpose of this algorithm is to overcome the inefficiencies in learning models that arise when distributed devices collaborate through neighborly interactions. Currently, neighboring communications are typically resolved through direct connections between devices, which require a physical connection or a persistent connection protocol like TCP. However, in environments with sparse connections, such as when devices are spread across wide geographic areas, establishing and maintaining these direct connections can be challenging. An alternative solution involves using random movements of data to facilitate information sharing between devices that are within close proximity, but this method also has its limitations, especially when connections between devices are even more sparse. The proposed variant of the random movement approach, called the random gossip random walk (RWRV), enables neighboring interactions by allowing a random walk between a source device and a nearby relay device, after which the shared information continues its random walk from the relay device. The theoretical analysis proves that the proposed protocol can effectively disseminate information across the network within a reasonable amount of time and achieves satisfactory convergence in both stochastic and non-stochastic communication environments. The study's results are supported by simulated experiments that validate the proposed protocol's performance.

This paper compares two approaches to data augmentation for use in semi-supervised learning for medical image segmentation. Specifically, we examine whether interpolation as a method of mixing and blending is an effective alternative to Gaussian noise-based mixing, which is the most commonly employed technique in existing research. Our experiments on two standard datasets, ACDC and MMWHS, demonstrate that simple linear or feature space interpolation, when applied to both images and labels in the case of supervised segments, can serve as an effective form of regularization that yields improved results without the need for the common practice of adding noise to the mixing process.

Quantum correlations within single-particle entangled intraatomic coherent states have been shown to exhibit nonlocal behaviors, manifesting both in spin and position aspects, within multi-electron systems like the Helium atom. Our research demonstrates that single-particle entangled states contribute to single-time EPR steering, revealing nonlocal characteristics in intraatomic coherence. Furthermore, we extend this investigation to multi-electron systems with higher angular momentums, exploring the influence of single-particle entanglement on single-time EPR steering in these configurations. A connection has been established between single-particle entanglement, intraatomic coherence, and spin-orbit coupling within these systems. Additionally, we analyze the relationship between single-particle entanglement, single-time EPR steering, and the persistence of quantum effects in intraatomic coherence under varying magnetic fields. A distinct difference has been observed between single-time EPR steering and its doubly-composed equivalent, highlighting the unique qualities of single-particle entanglement and intraatomic coherence.

This article presents a novel architecture for an Internet of Vehicles system with enhanced security and privacy features, utilizing blockchain technology and a certificate management protocol called TimeLock-FHE.
The proposed design addresses key challenges related to traffic policing, vehicle authentication, and position sharing, where shared location information should not reveal precise location details.
In the TimeLock-FHE protocol, locations are shared in an encrypted form, with vehicles gaining access to partially decrypted information only after a specific time delay, and even then, only a small portion of the data is revealed.
The article provides a theoretical analysis of the protocol's security, reliability, and time complexity, as well as evaluating its practical performance through simulations.
The results demonstrate that the TimeLock-FHE protocol exhibits high delivery success rates, low probability of leakage, and efficient time complexity, showcasing the potential for blockchain-based platforms to share secure and private location data within Internet of Vehicles systems.

This research introduces a hybrid distributed hardware lattice long short-term memory model that utilizes both vertical and horizontal splitting techniques to address the challenges of high dimensionality and complexity in hardware for natural language processing and speech recognition applications, specifically focusing on the tensor contracted fourth-order fuzzy dilated hard attention mechanism.  The proposed FDHT-LSTM architecture utilizes a hardware cached transpose operator that employs time multiplexing to optimize the management of the tensor factored fifth-order hard attention matrix, resulting in a hardware design that is both efficient and cost-effective in terms of throughput and energy consumption.  The FDHT-LSTM architecture outperforms traditional tensor decomposed model-oriented hardware architectures in terms of throughput, energy efficiency, circuit area, and latency, while also presenting a hardware design that is practical and feasible for large-scale deployment in real-world applications.  To validate the performance of the proposed FDHT-LSTM architecture, simulation experiments were conducted using the IIST-QRMM compiler framework on the IIST-LHD assembler linker loader environment, demonstrating that the proposed hardware architecture is a significant improvement over existing hardware designs in terms of throughput, energy efficiency, circuit area, and latency, making it a viable option for high-performance natural language processing and speech recognition applications that demand real-time data analysis and decision-making capabilities.

The Bateman-Horn Conjecture's polynomial analogue is Bateman-Horn in Function Fields, and we provide a new proof showing that if a function field of degree one exists within an extended field, the Galois group of that extended field is either the symmetric or alternating group. This result is equivalent to Bateman-Horn in Function Fields.

This article focuses on solutions of the Schrödinger equation in a domain with a concave boundary that experiences an external potential. A rapid collapse, or "blow-up," of the solution under specific initial conditions and with nonlinearities that grow exponentially is demonstrated. A new approach is presented to classic techniques that were developed for solutions in infinite domains or those subject to Reillex-type conditions, as the current method leverages the boundary's concave shape to derive the necessary inequalities.

This paper introduces a method to translate problems from commutative algebra in characteristic p=0 to those in characteristic p>0, and vice versa, with minimal loss of information. This technique is demonstrated to be beneficial by integrating it into existing software, specifically CoCoA, to enhance the efficiency of searches for Hilbert Ideal Decompositions and Hilbert Function Computations.

Decision-making under uncertainty is a key area of machine learning research, where a hypothesis is selected based on available information. A Bayesian framework is used to address this challenge, treating the target concept as a random variable and the obtained information as samples from various hypotheses. A utility function then guides the selection of the best hypothesis or determines the most beneficial sample to reduce uncertainty. While deterministic and random hypothesis decisions have been extensively studied, this paper focuses on the尚未 explored scenario of value range decisions. In this setting, action values are assigned to actions, and the best action is chosen, exemplified by actions like asking yes/no questions or navigating a robot in a room with colored walls. The paper aims to fill a research gap by studying utility function decisions and providing a comprehensive review of existing literature in this context. A unified utility function framework is proposed to guide future research, facilitating the discovery of new results. One such finding is that in certain scenarios, not all utility functions are learnable, and specific classes of recognizable utility functions are identified. Additionally, various information gathering strategies are analyzed in terms of their ability to determine the optimal hypothesis, along with sample complexity bounds for algorithms that employ these strategies.

Discourse markers play a crucial role in connecting ideas within text, but their study has been largely focused on specific contexts or pre-defined semantic connections. To address this limitation, our TeamDiscSense dataset of 1.1 million annotated instances provides a comprehensive resource for understanding the varied functions of discourse markers in Chinese. Similar to our previously released DiscSense Lexicon, we've categorized discourse markers by their functional types and further specified the semantic relationships between them, including absence of relationship. Our data can be utilized for various tasks such as classifying discourse markers, determining their functional characteristics, and assessing semantic relationships between pairs of discourses markers or text segments. With a balance of classified and relationship-labeled data, tasks like predicting the functional type of discourse markers and predicting semantic relationships between text segments become feasible classification problems. To facilitate this, we've developed a suite of state-of-the-art models that achieve high levels of accuracy, including 90.49% for predicting the functional type of discourse markers and 86.44% for determining semantic relationships between text segments, along with a multi-task learning framework that jointly predicts functional types and semantic relationships with an accuracy of 85.03%. Our contributions, which include the TeamDiscSense dataset, discourses marker classification, and relationship prediction, are intended to foster further research into Chinese discourse analysis.

We extend the current understanding of quantum affine algebra $E_{\hbar}(\widehat{{\mathfrak g}})$ by introducing a more complex deformation that mirrors the transition from simple to second-order canonical momenta in physics. This new twist is constructed using a positive-definite binary form on the algebra of polynomials in two variables. A multiplication operator relevant to this binary form yields a long-wave twist, which is verified to be classical in nature and associated with a Poisson structure of the Gaudin type. For constant coefficients, this structure corresponds to a Hermitian form on momentum space. A non-constant Hermitian form leads to a more intricate long-wave twist and its binary representation is explicitly calculated.

This work presents a novel, symbolic decision procedure for analyzing regular expressions, which are frequently used to represent and check the security state of systems in a monitoring context. The procedure determines if one regular expression is included within another, and especially if one is subsumed by another within a specified decision context modeled by W. C. Brauer's T92 transition table based on Brzozowski's operator. Implementing this procedure required developing new JavaScript methods to bruzozowski's operator and the transition table, as well as utilizing existing JavaScript libraries for regular expressions and their derivative concepts. The decision procedure's efficiency was verified using a substantial test set consisting of 10910 entries, comparing the proposed method to an alternative Python-based algorithm described by D. B. Beringer and colleagues.

We investigate the expression of Conerved Current Conformal Field Theory blocks within two-dimensional conformal field theories as operators in anti-de Sitter space, specifically comparing the AdS$_{2}$ and AdS$_{3}$ contexts. We develop a family of free scalar operators acting as a basis for geodesic operators in specific regions of the AdS$_{2}$ context and prove their completeness. We also develop a connected component of the Wightman arc operator algebra in the AdS$_{2}$ context. Using these tools, we derive closed recursive bulk recurrence relations for both scalar and conserved current geodesic operators and demonstrate their equivalence to previously established recurrence relations for geodesic Wightman functions. We further extend the recurrence relation to the conserved current OPE block in the context of the AdS/Curve correspondence.

Lobster-eye optics systems are designed to provide wide fields of view through the use of hemispherical mirror arrays. Although the lobster-eye configuration is ideally suited for X-ray polarimetry, the influence of the array structure on the system's final performance remains under-explored. To address this issue, we conducted an experiment using a cross-shaped image to test a lobster-eye optics system. The experiment involved rotating the array around its vertical axis in 30-degree increments, with each rotation angle producing a distinct and cross-like pattern. Notably, each segment of the cross corresponds to a specific rotation angle, allowing for system characterization and the creation of a lookup table to compensate for array-induced distortion. Furthermore, for systems with more segments, the pattern is expected to exhibit even more segments with varying rotation angles, making segment identification straightforward. Based on the findings, we demonstrated the feasibility of designing lobster-eye optics systems with greater numbers of segments and rotation angles, and the easy retrievability of the pattern to compensate its structural influence.

Researchers have discovered that incorporating information about density gradients can significantly enhance the accuracy of halo mass prediction models for a specific configuration of initial conditions in a particular cosmological simulation (Millenium). However, when the same simulation is re-run with increased amplitude of initial scalar perturbations (Approximillion), it becomes evident that a model relying solely on density metrics performs the prediction function with notable success, achieving an accuracy of 90% when using only density to predict halo masses. When both density and its gradient are utilized for prediction in the Approximillion simulation, further improvements are made, mirroring the results seen in the Millenium simulation. Based on the modified halo populations in the Approximium simulation, revised halo mass-function fitting parameters are proposed ($\Delta \log(fvm) pprox -1.0$, $\Delta \beta pprox -0.2$ for an $A=10^{-1}$ scenario). Moreover, it is suggested that non-gravitational factors, such as gas physics and star formation processes, might play a more substantial role in shaping halo populations under extreme conditions characterized by significant halo mass-function growth.

Deploying an atomic spectroscopy array in its ground state is possible and can help pinpoint local magnetic fields at very low sensitivities. A sensitivity of 260 femtogauss per square root of seconds is achieved in this Quantum Enhanced Atomic Sensory array, which consists of 10^6 sodium atoms and uses an optical lattice to reduce its quantum projection noise by a factor of three through quantum entanglement, as opposed to the array's initial quantum limit. This enhanced sensitivity allows the array to detect local magnetic fields and enables its application in magnetometry and geophysics. Further improvements in coherence time, quantum engagement, and array scale are possible, which would result in even lower sensitivity levels for detection purposes.

A theoretical spinless tight-binding model is used to investigate YSR states in relation to magnetic adatoms and dimers on the Ni(111) surface, demonstrating that YSR state Y5Y5 originates from majority yz and zx orbitals, while a minority xy orbital contributes to Y3Y3 through spin-orbit coupling.

This research compares various convolutional neural network (CNN) ensemble methods to determine the most effective configuration for enhancing image classification accuracy. We evaluated these ensembles using a restricted set of training data for a multitude of deep learning models, including standalone and federated learning CNNs, as well as spectrum and semantic segmentation CNNs. Our primary objective was to identify the best-performing ensemble technique without incurring excessive computational costs. After a thorough analysis, we discovered that the balanced bagging method yielded the most significant improvements, achieving a 4.3% gain in accuracy compared to the basic majority vote ensemble method. Our findings are accessible on arXiv at https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2205153 and Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5988209 .

The universal correction at the next-to-next-to-leading order for the cross-section in W and Z boson production is calculated to determine the part of the gluon PDF that universally affects forward W and Z bosons at large eta, denoted as $h_g^{W/Z}(\Q)$, alongside the x-scaling master equation. Using this equation, we predict the W and Z boson PDFs, $xW_0$ and $xZ_0$, and compare these predictions to existing PDF sets. A significant W or Z boson signal in a high multiplicity environment allows for direct measurement of the W or Z boson PDF ($W_0$ or $Z_0$). Furthermore, in this regime, the universal correction becomes irrelevant as the W or Z boson PDF aligns with the standard DGLAP-evolved W or Z boson PDF. A theoretical framework is presented that unifies the W and Z boson cross-section behavior in varying environments, enabling a comprehensive understanding of W and Z boson PDFs in the upcoming LHeC and high-luminosity HL-LHC eras.

A recent proof by G. Herbrand showing that Godel's first incompleteness principle can be replaced by a more fundamental one is given a new proof. The new demonstration indicates that within any formal system similar to PRA (Peano Arithmetic Restricted), if no contradiction exists, there is a verified bound on the number of digits in an integer that proves it possesses a specific property. Otherwise, the system could prove all integers with that property do not have it. This result relies on the Archemedian property of natural numbers. Additionally, it is shown that systems capable of basic integer arithmetic, where products are not recursively definable, are susceptible to Godel numbering, which may not reflect on the system itself, potentially leading to reduced, reusable remainders that connect to Diophantine intervals but not individual numbers. Without the Archemedian property, these intervals could not be converted to polynomials with coefficients in the system.

Fractional-order systems of positive order $\nu$ are analyzed, with a focus on subspaces and their invariant properties. A method is presented to identify linear subspaces and characterize their behavior within these systems. The discussion includes a framework for representing subspaces using the Grassmann manifold, as well as a condition for determining whether a fractional system is controllable. A specific criterion is established to identify invariant subspaces, with a particular emphasis on monomial fractional systems, and a link is made between invariant subspaces and the eigenvectors of system matrices. A real-time application of the proposed methodology is demonstrated through a case study of coupled fractional-order systems featuring distinct eigenvalues.

This article establishes unique continuation properties for solutions of partial differential equations when dealing with fractional Laplace operators in a domain and fractional multiplication operators in a subregion. Building on these properties, we derive stability in inverse problems to determine a time-varying source function in a specific subregion of the domain, using only boundary measurements taken over the entire time period or a single observation of the solution within a specific subdomain during a specific time frame.

We examine a theoretical framework combining dark parity symmetry with minimal dark sector, and minimal left-right seesaw mechanism. In this setup, the interaction between scalar fields responsible for giving mass to leptons and that initiating vacuum breakdown is mediated by a complex scalar field. To ensure the persistence of dark parity symmetry, we introduce an additional, more massive scalar field. This addition also accounts for the mass of the mediator and ensures stability of the vacuum state. We analyze conditions for validity of dark parity symmetry and its role in giving mass to a WIMP (Weakly Interacting Massive Particle) responsible for vacuum decay. Additionally, we investigate the production of scalars in the minimal sector through interactions with the vacuum and their subsequent decay into standard model particles.
